questions.q: In the mid-size company example, what happens when a customer who clicks a marketing email eventually becomes a sales deal?
options: They become a Lead, which Sales works into an Account, Contact, and Opportunity
They are automatically converted into a Case
Nothing changes in Salesforce until the deal closes
A new Salesforce org is created just for that customer
questions.explain: A marketing click typically creates a Lead, which Sales then works and converts into an Account, Contact, and Opportunity as the deal progresses.

questions.q: Why can the Sales team and Service team see completely different apps and Home pages while working on the exact same Account record?
options: Because they are actually in two separate Salesforce orgs
Because apps are just curated bundles of tabs for a job function — switching apps doesn't change the underlying org or data
Because Service reps aren't allowed to see Account records
Because Sales and Service always use different Salesforce editions
questions.explain: Apps only change which tabs are presented for a given job function — the underlying org, data, and records (like a shared Account) remain exactly the same.

questions.q: What stays consistent underneath every department's different app experience, according to this lesson?
options: Each department actually runs on a separate instance
One multitenant org, one edition and license set, and the same metadata-driven objects
Each department has its own separate set of standard objects
Nothing is shared; every department's data is fully isolated
questions.explain: Despite different apps and Home pages, every department shares one multitenant org, one edition and license set, and the same underlying metadata-driven objects and fields.

questions.q: What is an example given of an industry adapting Salesforce's standard model to its own needs?
options: A nonprofit using Accounts to represent donor households
Every industry is required to use Salesforce in an identical way with no customization
Only technology companies are permitted to use Salesforce
Nonprofits cannot use Salesforce at all
questions.explain: A nonprofit might repurpose the Account object to represent donor households — one example of how the same platform adapts to very different industries.

questions.q: What is the next course in the Salesforce Administrator path after Salesforce & CRM Foundations?
options: Hands-On Salesforce Environment
Advanced Apex Development
Salesforce Data Architecture
Tableau for Salesforce Analysts
questions.explain: Hands-On Salesforce Environment is the next course in the Salesforce Administrator path, where students set up and start working inside a real, free Salesforce environment of their own.
